drafted: 2026-10-29: fix sites read from the fixture source (the vulnerable statements; each function is the innermost enclosing def). Includes instances in introduction/mitre.py and dockerized_labs/, which the ground-truth docstring does not name (see each key's notes). Every quote checked by eval.devbench.check_keys. keys.name: SQL Injection via objects.raw()

fix_sites.quote: sql_query = "SELECT * FROM introduction_login WHERE user='"+name+"' AND password='"+password+"'"
fix_sites.why: POST 'name' and 'pass' are concatenated into a SQL string that login.objects.raw(sql_query) executes on line 162.

fix_sites.quote: sql_query = "SELECT * FROM introduction_sql_lab_table WHERE id='"+name+"'AND password='"+password+"'"
fix_sites.why: POST 'name' and 'pass' are concatenated into a SQL string that sql_lab_table.objects.raw(sql_query) executes on line 878.

keys.notes: Both SQLi labs are listed: 2017 sql_lab (routes sql_lab, sql_lab1) and 2021 injection_sql_lab (route injection_sql_lab). In sql_lab the raw query is only reached when login.objects.filter(user=name) finds the name (line 156), so 'name' must equal an existing user and the injectable input is effectively 'pass'. injection_sql_lab 864-878 also spans the seeding saves at 866-873 (kept so the site stays one statement range of 15 lines). No parameterised/secure variant of either lab exists in the repo. No +/-10 window overlaps another key.

fix_sites.quote: The company '{{query|safe}}' You searched for is not Part of FAANG

Only [a-zA-Z0-9] are stripped (line 129) and the rest is rendered inside a <script> block, so non-alphanumeric JavaScript survives.
User-derived 'code' is inserted into a JavaScript context, where HTML autoescaping does not neutralise it.
GET 'username' is passed unmodified to lab2.html, which prints it with |safe.
The |safe filter renders the reflected username as raw HTML.

keys.name: Cryptographic Failure (MD5 password hashing)

fix_sites.why: The login password is hashed with unsalted MD5 before comparison with the stored hash.
The login password is hashed with customHash (one unsalted SHA-256, reversed) before comparison.
customHash is a single unsalted SHA-256 with the hex string reversed -- a fast hash, not a password KDF.
The login password is hashed with unsalted MD5 before the CSRF_user_tbl lookup.
The admin role is read from a plaintext 'username|expire' cookie that carries no signature or encryption.
The auth cookie is issued as an unsigned, unencrypted 'username|expire' string.

keys.notes: Primary CWE-916 (password hash with insufficient computational effort) because every hash site hashes passwords with MD5 or one SHA-256 pass, unsalted; CWE-328/CWE-327/CWE-759 are listed as alternatives. crypto_failure_lab3 is PyGoat's Cryptographic Failure lab 3 (code comment 'based on CWE-319'); its flaw is an unsigned client cookie that sets the role, which could equally be filed under IDOR -- judgement call, kept in PyGoat's category. Excluded: auth_failure_lab3's sha256 at views.py:1194 (same weakness, but that function is an AUTHZ site); the dockerized broken_auth_lab md5 reset token (AUTHZ); auth_failure_lab2 uses argon2 PasswordHasher (not weak); the md5 hex literals at views.py 866-872 are seed data; challenge/models.py:28 hashes a flag, not a password. keys.name: Authentication Failure (weak/broken auth flow)

fix_sites.why: Stores the password in plaintext and then sets the account's userid as the only authentication cookie (line 291).
A GET logs the caller in as whichever account the client-supplied 'userid' cookie names, with no secret or server-side session.
Five wrong passwords lock the account for 1440 minutes, so anyone who knows the admin username can lock the real admin out.
Logout (a POST without credentials) only overwrites the cookie; the AF_session_id row is never deleted, so the old session_id stays valid.
The session token is an unsigned base64 of 'username:timestamp', so it can be forged.
The reset token is md5 of the email and current time, and is echoed back in the response (line 91).
The dashboard authenticates by base64-decoding the 'session' cookie and trusting the username before ':'.

keys.notes: Covers PyGoat's 2017 Broken Authentication lab (auth_lab; auth_home.html hint: think about cookies), the 2021 A7 labs 2 and 3 (a7.html: lab 2 asks to make the real admin unable to access the panel; lab 3 asks to reach a user's account after logout; A7_disscussion_api's expected fix is 'AF_session_id.objects.get(sesssion_id = cookie).delete()'), and the dockerized Flask broken_auth_lab (separate app; judgement call). PyGoat's A7 lab 1 is the 3-digit OTP brute force (Otp view via /bau_lab); it is listed under DESIGN-OTP because that item names the OTP, so one Otp finding cannot credit both -- reviewer may move it. auth_failure_lab3 also hashes with unsalted sha256 (1194) and raises KeyError for an unknown username at 1200. Not listed: hard-coded credentials in a1_broken_access_lab_1/2/3 (766, 806, 831-833), crypto_failure_lab3 (1072) and playground/A9/api.py (admin/admin); print(user_name,passwd) at 314. Window overlap: dashboard [101,122] vs MISCONFIG app.py:123 [113,133].

keys.name: Insecure Design (predictable OTP / ticket)

fix_sites.why: The OTP is a 3-digit value (900 possibilities) from the non-cryptographic random.randint.
OTP verification has no attempt limit and also accepts a match on the admin OTP row (id=2) regardless of the email cookie.
The 5-ticket cap is enforced per account only, so one person with several free accounts can take all 60 tickets.

keys.notes: Primary CWE-330 because the item is named for predictable/guessable values; the OTP flaw is a small value space plus no rate limiting (CWE-334/CWE-307) and the ticket flaw is business logic (CWE-799/CWE-837/CWE-840). Otp (route otp) is also PyGoat's 2021 A7 'Identification and Authentication Failures' lab 1 (a7.html: brute-force the 3-digit OTP, lack of rate limiting) -- judgement call to keep it here, not in AUTHZ. insec_desgine_lab (route insecure-design_lab) is PyGoat's Insecure Design lab (a11.html: get all the tickets; hint: logout and think). Not listed: gentckt (views.py 679-680) makes ticket codes with random.choices (CWE-338), but the lab text points at the per-account limit, and its window [670,690] would overlap LOGGING's a10_lab2 site [658,682]; reviewer may add it. Also not listed: the dockerized sensitive_data_exposure generate_api_key (random.choices) and broken_auth_lab's md5 reset token (in AUTHZ).

The exposed log records a login URL carrying a username and password in its query string.
Logs the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For value without neutralisation.

Log.info is a no-op, so log_function_target records nothing for GET/POST/PUT/PATCH requests.
Log.warning is a no-op.
Log.error is a no-op, so the unauthenticated DELETE in log_function_target goes unrecorded.

keys.notes: Not identifiable from requirements.txt alone: no line is marked, and confirming a version is known-vulnerable needs an advisory feed (pip-audit/OSV), which was not consulted. Both sites come from the repo's own A9 'Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities' lab material. Pillow is the weaker one: the lab text says 'Pillow 8.0.0' (a9.html:59, a9_lab2.html:38) while requirements.txt pins 9.4.0, so the repo does not establish that 9.4.0 is vulnerable -- reviewer should confirm or drop it. The A6 discussion test bench (apis.py:114) checks 'Pillow==8.0.0', 'PyJWT==2.4.0', 'requests==2.28.0', 'Django==4.0.4' against PyPI's vulnerability field; only PyJWT==2.4.0 equals a pin (requirements.txt:24) and the repo does not say which of them are vulnerable. The file has 34 lines, so the two windows ([9,29] and [17,37]) cover every line: any requirements.txt finding L1-matches. The dockerized labs' own requirements.txt files (e.g. sensitive_data_exposure django==3.2.18, requests==2.28.1; broken_auth_lab Flask==2.3.3, Werkzeug==2.3.7) were not assessed.
